cards.name: Backfire
cards.officialEffect: If a face-up FIRE monster(s) you control is destroyed and sent to the GY: Inflict 500 damage to your opponent.

cards.name: Balloon Lizard
cards.kind: Effect Monster / EARTH / Reptile / Level 4 / 500 ATK / 1900 DEF
cards.officialEffect: Put 1 counter on this card during each of your Standby Phases. When this card is destroyed, inflict damage to the controller of the card that destroyed it equal to the number of counters x 400 points.

design.backfire: One event snapshot may contain several simultaneously destroyed monsters; each face-up Backfire copy on that team's shared backrow emits one 500-damage packet if at least one face-up FIRE monster controlled by that team was sent to the GY. Face-down, non-FIRE, banished and non-GY destinations are excluded. Battle and effect destruction are both accepted.
design.balloonLizard: One counter per own Standby Phase, only while the card is face-up in the active controller team's Monster Zone. Duplicate event delivery is idempotent. On destruction, damage is 400 per recorded counter to the snapshotted controller team of the destroying card, not to the destroyed card's owner. Counters are removed when the card leaves the Monster Zone.
design.physicalOwnership: The adapter does not rewrite physical UIDs, hands, Decks, graveyards, or banished zones. The destroying-card controller is snapshotted by the event and cross-checked if that card remains on the shared field.
design.integration: Pure adapter only; shared resolver integration is withheld pending explicit M61 handoff.

tests: Backfire face-up FIRE monster sent to GY
simultaneous FIRE destruction: 500 per Backfire copy, not per monster
duplicate UID and invalid team rejection
counter cleanup after leaving Monster Zone
400 damage per counter to destroyer controller team

certification.reason: No resolver, metadata, certification, manifest, allowlist or catalog changes; adapter-only tests do not constitute an engine-v9 certification.

limitations: The adapters emit immutable damage packets; the central duel engine must apply them after an explicit M61 handoff.
Tests use structural TagDuel fixtures because these two cards are not yet enabled in the shared catalog.
This workflow does not simulate a full 2v2 duel through the live Discord gateway.
No card certification or inventory distribution is claimed.
